en.title: Maximum Tertile Gap After at Most K Increments or Decrements
en.description:
Each operation adds 1 to or subtracts 1 from any one element, at most K times in total. N is divisible by 3; maximize the N/3-th largest element minus the N/3-th smallest element.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol; ranges not given by the source are stated explicitly.
en.input: The first line contains N K; the second line contains N integers. N is a multiple of 3 in 3..150000, K is in 0..500000000, and the elements are in −300000000..300000000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: Example 1: both 6s must change to move the quantile by 1, so 3 steps can only increase the gap by 1. Example 2: the original gap is 2; lowering 1 to −1 makes the gap 4. Example 3: changing one 7 to 8 moves the upper quantile from 7 to 8 while the lower quantile stays at 7, for a gap of 1.
hints: After sorting, you only need to lower the maximum of the smallest N/3 numbers or raise the minimum of the largest N/3 numbers. On either side, the cost of increasing the gap by 1 equals the current size of the extreme group; since this cost grows monotonically as the group expands, merge the cost segments of both sides with a heap and buy the cheapest increments first.
